description: Deterministic test vectors for kxco-post-quantum. Run test/run-vectors.js to verify these match the library output bit-for-bit.
notes: ML-DSA-65 signatures are randomized — we cannot pin signature bytes. We pin keypair hashes and verify round-trip.
ML-KEM encapsulation is randomized — we pin keypair hashes and verify decapsulate round-trip in the runner.
All hex is lowercase. All UTF-8 strings are explicit.

deriveSeed.name: zero master, info=role-b, length=32 (different info → different seed)

mlDsa_sign_roundtrip.name: sign known message with keypair from zero master; verify true

mlKem_encapsulate_roundtrip.name: encapsulate to keypair from zero master; decapsulate recovers same secret

fingerprint.name: fingerprint of ML-DSA-65 platform pubkey from zero master

ml_dsa_verify.description: ML-DSA signature verification over the webhook envelope, for both parameter sets. The public key decides the set (1952 bytes = ML-DSA-65, 2592 bytes = ML-DSA-87, any other size refused). The signature must be the size of the key set (3309 / 4627 bytes). A header prefix (ml-dsa-65= or ml-dsa-87=) that disagrees with the key set is refused; a bare hex value takes the set from the key. Header value = header_prefix + signatures[signature].hex. Signatures are randomised, so these bytes were generated once and are pinned here; verification of them is deterministic.
ml_dsa_verify.generated_by: kxco-post-quantum 1.7.9 (mlDsa87.keypairFromMaster, mlDsa87.sign, mlDsa.keypairFromMaster, webhook.pqSign; signing backend: openssl 3.5.6 via node:crypto)
